questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the Ravana Phadi cave at Aihole.
1. Nataraja is the important structure at this site.
2. This Nataraja image is surrounded on the right by four large saptamatrikas and on the left by three large ones.
3. The figures have slim, graceful bodies with long oval faces.
4. The temple shows a distinct feature.
questions.solution:
1, 2 and 3
The Ravan Phadi cave, located in Aihole, Karnataka, is an example of early Chalukyan architecture. The first capital of the Chalukya Dynasty was Aihole which is clear from the inscriptions found in the caves of Aihole. The bronze sculpture of Nataraja was cast during the period of the Cholas dynasty.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Kailashnath Temple, Ellora.
1. It is built completely in the Dravidian style.
2. Its main deity is Lord Shiva.
3. This temple was carved out of a portion of a hill.
4. It was built during the Chola phase at Ellora.
Which of the given statements is correct?
questions.solution:
Only 1, 2 and 3
The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century. Located in Cave 16, it is dedicated to Lord Shiva and was carved from a single rock. Named after Mount Kailash, it is the largest of the 34 Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu cave temples at Ellora and was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1983.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Kushana dynasty:
Statement 1: Kujula Kadphises was the founder of the Kushana dynasty.
Statement 2: Vasudeva I was the last important ruler of the Kushana dynasty.
questions.option_1: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 correctly explains Statement 1
questions.option_2: Both statements are true, but Statement 2 does not explain Statement 1
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Both statements are true, but Statement 2 does not explain Statement 1
Kushan Dynasty (First-Third Century): Kanishka administered the territory from two capitals: Purushapura (now Peshawar in northern Pakistan) and Mathura. Vasudeva I was the last Kushana ruler.

questions.question: Kathasaritasagara, a collection of stories, was written in which of the following languages?
questions.solution:
Sanskrit
The Kathasaritsagara (Ocean of Story) was written in the 11th century by Somadeva.
Other Sanskrit Literature:
  • Buddhacarita - Ashvaghosa
  • Malavikagnimitram - Kalidasa
  • Harshacharita - Banabhatta

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Kushana dynasty is INCORRECT?
questions.option_1: The Kushanas were a major ruling group in the post-Mauryan period.
questions.option_2: Many Kushana rulers also adopted the title 'devaputra', or 'son of god'.
questions.option_3: The First Buddhist Council was organised by Kanishka.
questions.option_4: Asvaghosha, the author of the Buddhacharita, was the court poet of Kanishka.
questions.solution:
The First Buddhist Council was organised by Kanishka
The First Buddhist Council was held during the reign of King Ajatashatru of the Haryanka Dynasty in Rajgriha. Kanishka belonged to the Kushan dynasty, which was founded by Kujula Kadphises. The Fourth Buddhist Council was held under the patronage of Kanishka in Kashmir.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers is considered as the greatest king of Satavahana dynasty and is described as the destroyer of the Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas?
questions.solution:
Gautamiputra Satakarni
He is renowned for his military conquests and is described in the Nasik inscription as the "destroyer of the Sakas, Yavanas, and Pahlavas." He also used the title of 'Ekabrahaman,' which means the Peerless Brahman. Simuka was the founder of the Satavahana dynasty. Hala was the seventeenth king of the Satavahana Dynasty.

questions.question:
Match the following authors with their respective works:
List I (Authors)List II (Works)
1. Patanjali
2. Panini
3. Kautilya
4. Banabhatta		A. Ashtadhyayi
B. Mahabhashya
C. Arthashastra
D. Harshacharita
questions.solution:
1-B, 2-A, 3-C, 4-D
"The Yoga Sutra" was also written by Patanjali.
Authors and their books:

  • Vatsayana - "Kamasutra"
  • Vishnu Sharma - "Panchatantra"
  • Kautilya - "Arthashastra"
  • Panini - "Ashtadhyayi"
  • Megasthenes - "Indica"

  • Banabhatta - "Harshacharita", "Kadambari"

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties succeeded the Palas of Bengal?
questions.solution:
Senas Dynasty
A Hindu dynasty that ruled over eastern Bengal and western Bihar for about two centuries. Important Rulers - Vijaya Sena, Ballal Sena, Lakshmana Sena. Deva dynasty - Ruled over eastern Bengal after the Sena dynasty.

questions.question: Who had Sialkot as his capital?
questions.solution:
Menander
A Greek king who ruled over the Indo-Greek kingdom.
  • Demetrios (Greek king): His capital was Takshashila
  • Eucratides: Expanded the Indo-Greek territories into Bactria and the northern regions of India
  • Pushyamitra Sunga: An Indian king who ruled over the Sunga dynasty; his capital was Pataliputra

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the early history of the Vatapi (Badami) Chalukyas:
Statement 1: The Vatapi Chalukyas were originally tributary princes under the Kadamba dynasty.
Statement 2: The founder of the Kadamba dynasty was Mayurasharma, who ruled parts of present-day Karnataka.
questions.option_1: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 correctly explains Statement 1
questions.option_2: Both statements are true, but Statement 2 does not explain Statement 1
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Both statements are true, but Statement 2 does not explain Statement 1
The Vatapi (Badami) Chalukyas were first tributaries of the Kadambas of Banavasi (4th-6th century CE), founded by Mayurasharma. Later, under Pulakesin I (c. 543 CE), the Chalukyas declared independence and established Vatapi (Badami) as their capital, emerging as a major Deccan power.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of locations are famous for Buddhist railings and gateways?
questions.solution:
Bharhut and Amravati
Bharhut Stupa is located in Satna, Madhya Pradesh. It was discovered in a ruined state by Alexander Cunningham and his team. The discovered railing and gateway are now on display at the Indian Museum (Kolkata). Amravati Stupa was discovered by Colin Mackenzie (1797).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding forts in India:
Statement 1: Kangra Fort, also known as Nagarkot Fort, is considered the oldest dated fort in India.
Statement 2: Kangra Fort was built by Raja Man Singh of Amber in the 16th century.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
Kangra Fort, also called Nagarkot Fort, was built by Susharm Chand of the Katoch dynasty. In 1009 A.D., Mahmud of Ghazni plundered the Shahi treasury kept at Kangra in Himachal Pradesh. The Katoch dynasty traces its origin to the ancient Trigarta Kingdom mentioned in the Mahabharata.
Important forts in India include: Golconda Fort (Hyderabad), Mehrangarh Fort (Jodhpur, Rajasthan), Srirangapatna Fort (Karnataka), Panhala Fort (Maharashtra), and Daulatabad Fort (Aurangabad, Maharashtra).

questions.question: Brihat Samhita was the treatise of which of the following subjects?
questions.solution:
Astronomy
Brihat Samhita is the noted work of Varahamihira. It is an important encyclopedic text in Sanskrit.
Other Samhitas:
  • Jaya Samhita - Mahabharata
  • Charak Samhita - Medicinal Science
  • Sushruta Samhita - Book on Surgeries and related science

questions.question: Which ruler of the Chahamana dynasty made Ajmer his capital?
questions.solution:
Ajayaraja
Chahamanas or Chauhans dynasty: Chauhans of Delhi and Ajmer, also known as the Chahamanas of Shakkambhari, ruled over part of modern-day Rajasthan. Important Kings: Vasudeva, Ajayaraja, Arnoraja, Vigraharaja IV, Prithviraj Chauhan III, and Hariraja.

questions.question: Prithviraj Raso, an epic poem about the life of the 12th century Indian king, Prithviraj Chauhan, was written by:
questions.solution:
Chand Bardai
Indian Epics and writers:
  • Mahabharata - Sage Ved Vyasa
  • Ramayana - Valmiki
  • Raghuvamsa - Kalidasa
  • Buddhacharita - Asvogosha
  • Silapadikaram - Ilango Adigal (in Tamil)
  • Ramcharitmanas - Tulsidas (in Awadhi)
  • Kumarasambhava - Kalidasa (in Sanskrit)
  • Banabhatta wrote Harshacharita
  • Bharavi wrote Kiratarjuniya

questions.question: Siddheshwar Mahadev Temple in Bengal depicts the architecture of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
Pala Dynasty
Temples and their associated Dynasties:
  • Khajuraho Temple (Madhya Pradesh) - Bundelas or Chandelas
  • Kailash Temple (Maharashtra) - Rashtrakutas
  • Thousand Pillared Temple, Ramappa Temple (Telangana) - Kakatiyas
  • Brihadeeswara Temple (Tamil Nadu) - Cholas
  • Kailashnath Temple, Shore Temple (Tamil Nadu) - Pallavas
  • Dilwara Temple (Rajasthan) - Solankis
  • Virupaksha Temple (Karnataka) - Chalukyas
  • Sun Temple (Gujarat) - Solankis

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about ancient Indian literature:
Statement 1: Malavikagnimitra, a drama of the 5th century CE, was composed by Kalidasa, the court poet of Chandragupta II.
Statement 2: The Prayag pillar inscription was composed by Kalidasa in praise of Samudragupta.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
Malavikagnimitra was indeed written by Kalidasa, but the Prayag pillar inscription was composed by Harisena, not Kalidasa.

questions.question: The star-shaped temples were built during the reign of:
questions.solution:
Hoysala
Hoysala Architecture Temples: Aralaguppe is the temple dedicated to Lord Channakeshava (Vishnu). The temple was built during the rule of the Hoysala Empire King Vira Someshwara.

questions.question: Which of the following was the capital of the Hindu Shahi Kingdom?
questions.solution:
Waihind
Hindu Shahi kingdom was founded by Kallar. It ruled over Kabul and the old province of Gandhara from the decline of the Kushan empire. This kingdom was known as the Kabul Shahi dynasty.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Gahadavalas:
Statement 1: The Gahadavalas, also known as the Rathors of Kanauj, established their rule after the decline of the Pratiharas.
Statement 2: The last great Gahadavala ruler, Jai Chand, was defeated and killed in the Battle of Tarain (1191 AD) by Prithviraj Chauhan.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
The Gahadavalas ruled Kanauj after the decline of the Pratiharas, but Jai Chand was killed in the Battle of Chandawar (1194 AD) by Mohammad Ghor, not in the Battle of Tarain by Prithviraj Chauhan.

questions.question: Alvars were the devotees of which South Indian cult?
questions.solution:
Vaishnavism
Nayanars and Alvars saints belonged to South India. Some famous Vaishnava devotees: Ramanuja, Madhvacharya, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Nimbarkacharya.
  • Jainism - Devotees of Jainism are called Jains such as Rishabhadeva, Parshvanath, Bhadrabahu
  • Shaktism - Devotees of Goddess Shakti
  • Saivism - Devotees of Lord Shiva (Nayanars)

questions.question: The Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana in the ______ century AD.
questions.solution:
7th
Travellers Who Visited India:
  • Hiuen Tsang (China) - During the reign of Harshavardhana (7th century)
  • Al Biruni (Khwarizm, present-day Uzbekistan) - In 11th century during the reign of Sultan Mahmood Ghaznavi
  • Ibn Battuta (Morocco) - During the reign of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq
  • Marco Polo (Italy) - During the reign of Pandya Kingdom
  • Megasthenes (Greece) - During the reign of Chandragupta Maurya
  • Abdur Razzaq (Persia) - During the reign of Deva Raya II (Sangama dynasty)
  • Fa Hien (China) - During the reign of Chandragupta II
  • Al Masudi (Arab) - In 10th century AD

questions.question: The rulers of which of the following Rajput dynasties patronised Jainism and one of them is reported to have accepted Jainism under the influence of a Jain scholar Hemachandra?
questions.solution:
Chalukya
Pratihara dynasty - Nagabhatta I was the founder. The Pratiharas who ruled over Kannauj for a long time are also called Gurjara-Pratiharas. Paramara dynasty - Founded by Upendra or Krishnaraja. Capital: Ujjain, Later - Dharan Nagari (Dhar).

questions.question: Alha and Udal, who gave stiff resistance to the enemy, belonged to which of the following Rajput States?
questions.solution:
Chandella (Founder - Nannuk)
They were originally vassals of the Gurjara-Pratiharas. The Chandelas initially ruled as feudatories of the Gurjara-Pratiharas of Kanyakubja (Kannauj). Original capital - Khajuraho. The last King of this dynasty - Paradidev (Parmadi). His generals - Alha and Udal. Battle of Mahoba: Fought between Paradidev and Prithviraj Chauhan III in 1182 AD.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Pala Dynasty:
Statement 1: The Pala rulers, beginning with Gopala in 750 AD, were great patrons of Jainism.
Statement 2: The Pala rulers were staunch supporters of Mahayana Buddhism.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
Pala Dynasty - Founded by Gopala in 750 AD. They were staunch supporters of Mahayana Buddhism. They were in a tripartite struggle between the Palas, the Pratiharas and the Rashtrakutas for the control of Kanauj and North India.

questions.question: Who among the following was the author of the play 'Mirchchhakatika'?
questions.solution:
Shudraka
Mirchchhakatika play was translated into English by Arthur W. Ryder in 1905 as "The Little Clay Cart". Other Sanskrit plays of Shudraka: "Vinavasavadatta", "Padmaprabhritaka", "a bhana" (short one-act monologue).

questions.question: The Ashtadhyayi of Panini is a renowned work on
questions.solution:
Sanskrit Grammar
Ancient Authors and books:
  • (Kautilya) Chanakya's work - "Arthashastra" (on statecraft, political science, economic policy and military strategy)
  • Maharshi Charak - "Charaka Samhita" (a famous text of Ayurveda)
  • "Sushruta Samhita" - A comprehensive textbook on medicine and surgery

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Shunga Dynasty:
Statement 1: Pushyamitra Shunga was the last ruler of the Shunga dynasty.
Statement 2: Devabhuti, assassinated by his minister Vasudeva Kanva, was the last ruler of the Shunga dynasty.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
Devabhuti was assassinated by his minister (Vasudeva Kanva).
Other Kings of Shunga Dynasty: Pushyamitra Shunga (Founder of Shunga Dynasty), Agnimitra, Vasujyeshtha, Vasumitra, Bhagabhadra.
  • Shashanka: The first king of ancient Bengal, governed the Gauda Kingdom from 600 to 625 AD
  • Bhavabhuti: A famous Sanskrit playwright who wrote famous plays like Mahaviracharita, Malatimadhava etc.
